sourceCheck: The certification page links to a standard exam guide with 4 sections weighted ~20%, ~30%, ~30%, and ~20%. All 12 supplied subsection headings match. The current rename page confirms Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Runtime, and Workbench names. Gemini Cloud Assist is Preview; Application Design Center, Cloud Hub, and Database Center are GA, although each has individual Preview features. Google Antigravity is GA. Gemini CLI has a stable release channel, but its Google Cloud overview gives no product-wide GA or Preview label. I found current documentation for every product named in the guide. Current billing documentation distinguishes alerts-only budgets, which do not cap spending, from separate Preview spend cap budgets.

cards.statement: Resource Manager folders can sit below a project in the resource hierarchy.
cards.explanation: A folder belongs under an organization or another folder. Projects can sit under folders, but they do not contain Resource Manager folders.
cards.misconception: Projects can be parents of Resource Manager folders.

cards.statement: An organization policy on a folder applies to the projects beneath that folder.
cards.explanation: Organization Policy constraints set on a folder are inherited by its descendants, including projects beneath it.

cards.statement: A project IAM role granted to a Google group applies to each of its members.
cards.explanation: A role granted to a Google group applies to its members, so group membership can manage who receives the project role.

source.title: Create and manage Google groups in the Google Cloud console

cards.statement: A project IAM role can authorize creation of Cloud Identity groups.
cards.explanation: Google Workspace group permissions govern who creates Cloud Identity groups, including when creation happens in the Google Cloud console.
cards.misconception: Project IAM roles control Cloud Identity group administration.

source.title: Create and manage Google groups in the Google Cloud console

cards.statement: Google Cloud Directory Sync can provision Active Directory groups into Cloud Identity.
cards.explanation: Google Cloud Directory Sync provisions users and, optionally, groups from Active Directory into Cloud Identity or Google Workspace.

cards.statement: The gcloud services command group enables APIs for a selected Google Cloud project.
cards.explanation: The gcloud services enable command enables a named service for the current project.

cards.statement: A Cloud Monitoring metrics scope can include metrics stored in other projects.
cards.explanation: The scoping project can chart and alert on time series stored in other projects added to its metrics scope.

cards.statement: A project quota increases as soon as a user submits its adjustment request.
cards.explanation: Cloud Quotas evaluates adjustment requests and can deny them. Submission alone does not increase the quota.
cards.misconception: Submitting a quota adjustment immediately grants the requested capacity.

cards.statement: A standalone Google Cloud organization requires a Cloud Identity account for its creation.
cards.explanation: Google Cloud creates a standalone organization for an eligible signup using a Google email address, with no Cloud Identity account required.
cards.misconception: Every organization must be backed by Cloud Identity.
cards.volatilityNote: Standalone organization signup and eligibility may evolve.

cards.statement: The gcloud compute regions list command reports machine-type availability by zone.
cards.explanation: Use gcloud compute machine-types list to check which zones support a machine type. The regions list reports regional information such as status and quotas.
cards.misconception: Listing regions also checks zonal machine-type support.

cards.statement: Cloud Asset Inventory searches resources within a project, folder, or organization scope.
cards.explanation: Cloud Asset Inventory limits a resource search to the project, folder, or organization chosen as its scope.

cards.statement: Workforce Identity Federation stores external users as Cloud Identity accounts.
cards.explanation: Workforce Identity Federation authenticates users through an external identity provider without synchronizing them into Cloud Identity accounts.
cards.misconception: Workforce federation provisions a Google-managed user for each external user.

cards.statement: A Cloud Billing account can collect usage charges from several projects.
cards.explanation: One Cloud Billing account accrues charges for the projects linked to it, and an account can link to multiple projects.

source.title: Enable, disable, or change billing for a project

cards.statement: A project linked to a suspended Cloud Billing account keeps billing enabled.
cards.explanation: Billing is enabled only when the linked Cloud Billing account is active and in good standing. A suspended account leaves linked projects without enabled billing.
cards.misconception: A billing-account link is sufficient even when the account is suspended.

source.title: Verify the billing status of your projects

cards.statement: Moving a project to another Cloud Billing account transfers its earlier charges.
cards.explanation: Charges incurred before a project changes billing accounts remain on its former Cloud Billing account, even if they appear in transaction history later.
cards.misconception: Relinking a project moves its previous usage charges to the new account.

source.title: Enable, disable, or change billing for a project

cards.statement: A project Owner can link the project to any Cloud Billing account.
cards.explanation: Changing a project's Cloud Billing account requires project permissions and permissions on the relevant billing accounts; project ownership alone does not authorize an arbitrary target account.
cards.misconception: Project ownership grants access to every potential billing account.

source.title: Enable, disable, or change billing for a project

cards.statement: Cloud Billing budgets accept project and service filters for cost alerts.
cards.explanation: An alerts-only budget can narrow the costs it monitors to selected projects and services.

source.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

cards.statement: An alerts-only Cloud Billing budget pauses project usage at its threshold.
cards.explanation: An alerts-only budget sends alerts but does not pause services or stop billing when a threshold is met.
cards.misconception: A budget alert acts as an automatic spending cap.

source.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

cards.statement: A Cloud Billing budget alert can trigger from forecasted spend.
cards.explanation: Cloud Billing budget threshold rules can evaluate either actual spend or forecasted spend.

source.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts

cards.statement: Cloud Billing budgets publish programmatic notifications to a configured Pub/Sub topic.
cards.explanation: Connecting a Pub/Sub topic to a Cloud Billing budget delivers programmatic budget-status notifications to that topic.

cards.statement: Cloud Billing exports usage and cost data to a BigQuery dataset.
cards.explanation: Cloud Billing data export writes usage and cost data into BigQuery tables for analysis.

source.title: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery

cards.statement: Standard usage cost export identifies the cost of each Compute Engine VM.
cards.explanation: The detailed usage cost export adds resource-level cost information where available. The standard usage cost export reports broader billing dimensions.
cards.misconception: Standard billing export has the same resource-level detail as detailed export.

source.title: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery

cards.statement: Cloud Billing pricing export requires the BigQuery Data Transfer Service API.
cards.explanation: The project containing the pricing-export dataset needs the BigQuery Data Transfer Service API enabled.
cards.volatilityNote: The setup dependencies for billing exports may change.

source.title: Set up Cloud Billing data export to BigQuery

cards.statement: Cloud Billing creates the BigQuery dataset when usage export is enabled.
cards.explanation: You create the BigQuery dataset first, then configure Cloud Billing to export data into it.
cards.misconception: Enabling billing export also provisions its destination dataset.

source.title: Set up Cloud Billing data export to BigQuery

cards.statement: Compute Engine custom machine types let users choose vCPU count and memory.
cards.explanation: A custom machine type specifies vCPU count and memory for supported Compute Engine machine series, subject to valid combinations.

source.title: Create a VM with a custom machine type

cards.statement: With OS Login enabled, Compute Engine accepts SSH keys stored in VM metadata.
cards.explanation: With OS Login enabled, Compute Engine uses keys associated with the user's Google identity and stops accepting SSH keys from project or instance metadata.
cards.misconception: OS Login supplements metadata-based SSH keys.

cards.statement: Compute Engine Spot VMs can run for a maximum of 24 hours.
cards.explanation: Spot VMs have no fixed maximum runtime unless you configure one. The 24-hour limit belongs to preemptible VMs.
cards.misconception: The preemptible VM runtime limit also applies to Spot VMs.

cards.statement: Regional Persistent Disk replicates a disk across two Google Cloud regions.
cards.explanation: Regional Persistent Disk replicates data between two zones within one region, protecting against a zonal failure.
cards.misconception: Regional Persistent Disk replication crosses region boundaries.

cards.statement: Google Cloud Hyperdisk lets users change provisioned performance while a volume is in use.
cards.explanation: Hyperdisk supports changing provisioned IOPS or throughput on an in-use volume, according to the Hyperdisk type.

cards.statement: An autoscaled managed instance group creates VMs from an instance template.
cards.explanation: A managed instance group uses an instance template for its VMs; its autoscaler adds or removes instances according to the configured policy.

source.title: Create a MIG with autoscaling enabled

cards.statement: GKE Autopilot requires users to create node pools before deploying workloads.
cards.explanation: GKE Autopilot manages and provisions worker nodes for deployed workloads; users do not create node pools first.
cards.misconception: Autopilot has the same user-managed node-pool setup as GKE Standard.

cards.statement: A regional GKE cluster replicates its control plane across zones in one region.
cards.explanation: A regional GKE cluster keeps control-plane replicas in multiple zones of the selected region to reduce the impact of a zonal failure.

cards.statement: GKE private nodes receive external IP addresses for outbound connectivity.
cards.explanation: GKE private nodes receive internal IP addresses and have no external IP addresses.
cards.misconception: Private GKE nodes still receive public addresses for outbound traffic.

cards.statement: kubectl requires gke-gcloud-auth-plugin to authenticate to GKE clusters.
cards.explanation: GKE uses gke-gcloud-auth-plugin to provide authentication tokens to kubectl and other Kubernetes clients.

source.title: Install kubectl and configure cluster access

cards.statement: Cloud Run functions use Eventarc to receive Cloud Storage object events.
cards.explanation: Event-driven Cloud Run functions receive Cloud Storage events through Eventarc triggers.

cards.statement: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform deploys agents to user-managed GKE clusters.
cards.explanation: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is a fully managed runtime that deploys and scales agent applications while abstracting the underlying infrastructure.
cards.misconception: Using Agent Runtime means operating the agent's GKE cluster.
tags: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
cards.volatilityNote: Agent Platform runtime packaging and deployment options are evolving.

cards.statement: Cloud SQL can host MariaDB as a managed database engine.
cards.explanation: Cloud SQL offers managed MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server engines; MariaDB is not among its supported engines.
cards.misconception: MariaDB is a Cloud SQL engine because of its relationship to MySQL.
cards.volatilityNote: Cloud SQL's supported engine list may expand.

cards.statement: BigQuery batch load jobs ingest files stored in Cloud Storage into a table.
cards.explanation: A BigQuery batch load job reads supported source files from Cloud Storage and loads them into a BigQuery table.

cards.statement: Firestore multi-region locations place read-write replicas in separate regions.
cards.explanation: A Firestore multi-region location stores read-write replicas across regions so the database can continue serving data after a regional loss.

cards.statement: Spanner Enterprise edition provides multi-region instance configurations.
cards.explanation: Spanner multi-region instance configurations are available in Enterprise Plus edition.
cards.misconception: Spanner Enterprise includes the multi-region configurations of Enterprise Plus.
cards.volatilityNote: Spanner's edition feature matrix may change.

cards.statement: Bigtable orders rows by the lexicographic sort of their row keys.
cards.explanation: Bigtable sorts rows lexicographically by row key, so key design affects which related rows a range read reaches.

cards.statement: A Dataflow streaming job reading Pub/Sub ends after consuming the messages present at launch.
cards.explanation: Pub/Sub is a continuously updating source for a Dataflow streaming pipeline; the job continues processing newly arriving messages.
cards.misconception: A streaming job processes its initial backlog and then completes like a batch job.

cards.statement: Pub/Sub deletes an unacknowledged message when its acknowledgment deadline expires.
cards.explanation: When an acknowledgment deadline expires, Pub/Sub attempts to redeliver the unacknowledged message.
cards.misconception: An acknowledgment deadline is a message-deletion deadline.

cards.statement: Cloud Storage Archive can retrieve objects through an offline restore job.
cards.explanation: Cloud Storage Archive objects remain online and available within milliseconds; reads do not require an offline restore job.
cards.misconception: Archive objects need rehydration before they can be read.

cards.statement: Filestore supports NFSv3 file shares for Compute Engine application VMs.
cards.explanation: Filestore supports NFSv3 across its service tiers and can serve files to Compute Engine VM clients.

cards.statement: Storage Transfer Service moves on-premises file data into Cloud Storage.
cards.explanation: Storage Transfer Service supports transfers from on-premises storage into Cloud Storage.

cards.statement: A dual-region Cloud Storage bucket confirms uploads after replication to both regions.
cards.explanation: A successful upload confirms redundancy within the initial region. Cloud Storage replicates the object to the second region asynchronously.
cards.misconception: Successful upload means cross-region replication has already finished.

cards.statement: Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka sizes its broker count from cluster vCPU capacity.
cards.explanation: When creating a cluster, you specify total vCPU count and memory; Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka provisions the broker count from the vCPU count.
tags: Google Cloud Managed Service for Apache Kafka
cards.volatilityNote: Managed Kafka cluster-sizing behavior may evolve.

source.title: Managed Service for Apache Kafka overview
